question.text: What proportion of global fish production will be from aquaculture in 2040?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the percentage of world production of fish from aquaculture in comparison to the total world production of fish from aquaculture and capture combined, in 2040, according [the OECD Data Explorer platform](https://data-explorer.oecd.org/vis?fs[0]=Topic%2C1%7CAgriculture%20and%20fisheries%23AGR%23%7CAgricultural%20trade%20and%20markets%23AGR_TRD%23\&fs[1]=Commodity%2C2%7CAll%20Commodities%23_T%23%7CAgriculture%252C%20forestry%20and%20fishery%20products%23CPC_0%23%7CFish%20and%20other%20fishing%20products%23CPC_04%23\&pg=0\&fc=Commodity\&snb=5\&si=2\&vw=tb\&df[ds]=dsDisseminateFinalDMZ\&df[id]=DSD_AGR%40DF_OUTLOOK_2023_2032\&df[ag]=OECD.TAD.ATM\&df[vs]=1.0\&dq=W%2BOECD.A.CPC_EX_AC%2BCPC_EX_FHC...\&pd=%2C\&to[TIME_PERIOD]=false).
question.fine_print:
If the OECD ceases reporting world production of fish or significantly changes its criteria of recording such that previous reporting is not comparable, this question will be **annulled**. However, if another organisation takes over such reporting, that other source can be used for resolution as long as reporting is comparable.

*Given the Animal Futures Tournament timeframe, scores from this question will not be included in the tournament leaderboard. However participants are required to predict on at least two of the three long-term questions, as per the tournament rules.*

research:
I couldn't retrieve the resolution data directly. Every source projects aquaculture's share rising slowly: from about 52-53% now to about 56% by 2034-2035. No published source gives a figure for 2040.

## 1. Resolution source
- I couldn't reach the OECD Data Explorer or its data API: the page loads by script and the API returned 404/403. The question links to the **2023-2032** Outlook dataset. In that dataset, 2024 is a modelled year, not an observed one. The question background reports 2024 as 96,456 kt farmed and 88,755 kt wild-caught, which gives a 52.1% aquaculture share. I could not verify those figures myself.
- Each OECD-FAO Outlook only projects about 10 years ahead. A 2040 value would first appear in about the 2030-2039 edition, published around mid-2030. The 2040 figure will probably keep being revised until the final data is in. Which dataset edition counts for resolution is not clear.
- 2026-06: The newest edition, the OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2026-2035, says aquaculture rises from 53% of fisheries and aquaculture production in 2023-25 to 56% in 2035. Total production goes from 194 Mt to 216 Mt (live weight) and aquaculture output reaches 121 Mt, up 18%. [OECD chapter](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2026-2035_47874669-en/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products-for-human-consumption_be23d26b.html); [PDF](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2026/06/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2026-2035_5610f218/47874669-en.pdf)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles the question. Resolution is about 13 years away.
- 2026-06: FAO's SOFIA 2026 report puts 2024 aquaculture at about 53% of aquatic animal production (about 195 Mt total) and capture at about 92 Mt. Capture has stayed between 86 and 94 Mt since the late 1980s. [FAO GLOBEFISH](https://www.fao.org/in-action/globefish/news-events/news/news-detail/global-aquatic-food-trade---the-latest-findings-from-sofia-2026/en); [Aquafeed](https://www.aquafeed.co.uk/fao-sofia-2026-highlights-aquacultures-role/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Peru's fishing exports are expected to fall in 2026 because of El Niño. Boats have been kept in port since late April 2026, and the start of the 2027 anchovy season is uncertain. Lower anchovy catch pushes the aquaculture share up for that year. [Gestión](https://gestion.pe/economia/exportaciones-pesqueras-de-peru-cerraran-este-ano-en-rojo-por-el-impacto-de-el-nino-noticia/)
- 2026-11-03: Peruvian fishing exports for January-August 2026 were US$2.98bn, down 13.3% year on year. [La República](https://larepublica.pe/economia/2026/11/03/exportaciones-pesqueras-caerian-en-2026-por-el-nino-envios-retrocedieron-133-hasta-agosto-hnews-134838)
- 2026-11-04: Brazil's aquaculture in federal waters hit a record 179,600 t in 2025, up 20.9%. This is tiny on a global scale. [Tribuna PR](https://www.tribunapr.com.br/noticias/economia/producao-de-peixes-em-aguas-federais-cresce-209-e-bate-recorde/)
- 2026-06: The 2026-2035 Outlook says aquaculture growth is slowing, including in China, and that wild-caught fish going to fishmeal and fish oil will be 16.0-18.2 Mt in 2035 depending on El Niño/La Niña conditions. [IFFO](https://www.iffo.com/summary-oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2026-2035)
- 2026-06: SOFIA 2026 projects 214 Mt of aquatic animals in 2034: about 119 Mt from aquaculture (+16%) and 95 Mt from capture (+3%), which is a 56% aquaculture share. [Fisheries India](https://fisheriesindia.com/2026/10/fao-sofia-2026-global-fisheries-output-hits-235m-tonnes.html)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- 2022: Aquaculture overtook capture for the first time, with 94.4 Mt (51%) against 92.3 Mt. FAO says aquaculture has grown about 5% a year since 2000. [FAO](https://www.fao.org/newsroom/detail/fao-report-global-fisheries-and-aquaculture-production-reaches-a-new-record-high/en)
- Older projections have edged up with each edition:
  - 2023-2032 Outlook: 50% in the base period, 55% in 2032. [Fish Farming Expert](https://www.fishfarmingexpert.com/agricultural-outlook-2023-2032-oecd-fao-aquaculture-prediction-united-nations/salmonids-will-swim-with-the-tide-of-rising-aquaculture-production/1542209)
  - SOFIA 2024: 51% in 2022, 54% in 2032. [FAO](https://openknowledge.fao.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/1273bc36-339b-43d2-8163-af4d805f2ad2/content/sofia/2024/fisheries-aquaculture-projections.html)
  - 2025-2034 Outlook: 52% in the base period, 56% in 2034, with 212 Mt total. [OECD](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2025-2034_601276cd-en/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products_ed13346f.html)
- The projected pace is about 0.3-0.4 percentage points a year, roughly a third of the pace of the 2010s. My arithmetic, not a source forecast: continuing 2025-2035 Outlook pace in a straight line to 2040 gives roughly 57-58%.
- Year-to-year swings mostly come from capture, especially the Peruvian anchovy catch. An El Niño year can cut several Mt of capture and add about 1 percentage point to the aquaculture share for that year.
- Reasons the Outlooks give for slower growth: smaller productivity gains, stricter environmental rules and fewer suitable sites. Asia makes up about 88% of aquaculture output and China about 53%. [OECD 2025-2034](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2025-2034_601276cd-en/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products_ed13346f.html)

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the prediction-market prices supplied match this question. They cover catfish, GDP, LNG and similar. I found nothing on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus about global aquaculture share.
- I found no expert projection of the share for 2040. The longer-range sources I found don't give a share either:
  - DNV expects marine seafood production up about 20% by 2050, with marine aquaculture doubling and capture flat. [DNV PDF](https://vakbladvoedingsindustrie.nl/storage/app/media/Rapporten/rapporten%202024/VOE-2024-JAN-DNV.pdf)
  - WRI estimates aquaculture would need to reach about 140 Mt by 2050 to meet demand. [WRI](https://www.wri.org/research/improving-productivity-and-environmental-performance-aquaculture)

## 6. Upcoming events that could move the outcome
- Each mid-year OECD-FAO Outlook, 2027 through 2039, will extend and revise the projection. The first edition to include 2040 is likely the one published around 2030.
- Each SOFIA report every two years (next around 2028) will update the observed data.
- El Niño/La Niña cycles matter: the 2026 El Niño may weigh on Peru's anchovy quotas into 2027, and a 2039-2040 event could swing the final value.
- Slower growth in China's aquaculture or new environmental limits would lower the share. Faster aquaculture growth in Africa, South and Southeast Asia, or Latin America would raise it. Changes in fishing rules (for example, fisheries subsidy rules at the WTO) and climate effects on capture would also matter.
- If the OECD changes how it counts production (for example, whether algae is included) or which dataset is used, the question could be annulled.

I couldn't fetch any OECD or FAO page directly (all returned 403), so the figures below come from search-engine extracts of those pages and from the question text.

## 1. Resolution source
- Undated, as given in the question: the linked OECD dataflow is `DSD_AGR@DF_OUTLOOK_2023_2032`, from the OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2023-2032. It reports world aquaculture (CPC_EX_AC) and capture (CPC_EX_FHC). The question says its 2024 values are 96,454.48 kt aquaculture and 88,754.90 kt capture, a 52.1% aquaculture share. That 2024 number is a projection from the 2023 edition, not an observed figure. I could not check the values myself: the Data Explorer page came back empty and the SDMX API returned 403. [OECD Data Explorer](https://data-explorer.oecd.org/vis?df[ds]=dsDisseminateFinalDMZ&df[id]=DSD_AGR%40DF_OUTLOOK_2023_2032&df[ag]=OECD.TAD.ATM&df[vs]=1.0)
- **The 2040 value does not exist yet in any OECD dataset.** Each Outlook covers only 10 years: the 2023 edition ends in 2032, and the newest one (2026-2035) ends in 2035. A 2040 figure would most likely first appear in the 2031-2040 edition, expected around mid-2031. Actual 2040 data would not be published until about 2042. The resolver will have to choose which edition to use.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The share has been rising slowly, and the official projections stop at 2035.
- 2026-06 (SOFIA 2026, FAO's State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture report): in 2024, farmed aquatic animals reached 103 Mt, or 53% of aquatic animal production. Wild catch was 92 Mt, and capture has stayed between 86 and 94 Mt since the late 1980s. Aquaculture first overtook capture in 2021. FAO's totals are larger than OECD's, so the definitions differ somewhat. [DevelopmentAid](https://www.developmentaid.org/news-stream/post/208087/sofia-2026-global-fisheries-and-aquaculture-production-reaches-new-highs-report); [Mongabay](https://news.mongabay.com/2026/06/aquatic-animal-and-terrestrial-meat-trades-now-almost-on-par-fao-report-finds/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Spain's farmed fish output was 79,886 t, 24.4% of the EU total. [Diario de Sevilla](https://www.diariodesevilla.es/gente/acuicultura-haya-pescado_0_2008421342.html)
- 2026-11-04: Peru's fish exports are expected to end 2026 down because of El Niño. If the first 2027 anchovy season is delayed or gets low quotas, fleets will have stayed in port since late April 2026. A weak anchovy year lowers world capture and pushes the aquaculture share up temporarily. [Gestión](https://gestion.pe/economia/exportaciones-pesqueras-de-peru-cerraran-este-ano-en-rojo-por-el-impacto-de-el-nino-noticia/)
- 2026-11-03: Peru's fish exports for January-August 2026 were down 13.3% year on year. [La República](https://larepublica.pe/economia/2026/11/03/exportaciones-pesqueras-caerian-en-2026-por-el-nino-envios-retrocedieron-133-hasta-agosto-hnews-134838)
- 2026-11-04: Aquaculture in Brazil's federal waters hit a record 179,600 t in 2025, up 20.9%. [Tribuna PR](https://www.tribunapr.com.br/noticias/economia/producao-de-peixes-em-aguas-federais-cresce-209-e-bate-recorde/)
- 2026-06-29: The OECD-FAO Outlook 2026-2035 was released.
  - Aquaculture's share is projected to rise from 53% in the base period to 56% in 2035.
  - Total output goes from 194 Mt to 216 Mt, with aquaculture at 121 Mt, up 18%. Aquaculture grew 51% over the previous decade, so growth is slowing.
  - China's share of aquaculture falls to 55%.
  - [OECD-ilibrary](https://www.oecd-ilibrary.org/en/publications/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2026-2035_47874669-en/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products-for-human-consumption_be23d26b); [WAM](https://www.wam.ae/en/article/17ar0fm-global-agricultural-fisheries-production-projected)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- Historical aquaculture share of aquatic animal production (FAO): about 4-5% in 1950-1970, about 20% in the 1990s, about 27% in 2000 and 32% in 2003. It reached 44% in the 2010s, about 49% in 2020, 51% in 2022 and 53% in 2024. [FAO SOFIA 2024](https://openknowledge.fao.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/1273bc36-339b-43d2-8163-af4d805f2ad2/content/sofia/2024/world-fisheries-aquaculture-production.html); [FAO](https://www.fao.org/4/af053e/AF053E06.htm)
- Rough pace: about 1+ percentage point a year in the 2000s, about 0.5-1 pp a year in the 2010s, and about 0.3-0.4 pp a year in the official 2025-2035 projections.
- 2025-07 (Outlook 2025-2034): 52% in the base period, 56% in 2034. Total 212 Mt, aquaculture 118 Mt, capture 94 Mt. [OECD](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/2025/07/oecd-fao-agricultural-outlook-2025-2034_3eb15914/full-report/fish-and-other-aquatic-products_ed13346f.html)
- 2024 (SOFIA 2024): 51% in 2022, projected 54% in 2032. [FAO projections](https://openknowledge.fao.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/1273bc36-339b-43d2-8163-af4d805f2ad2/content/sofia/2024/fisheries-aquaculture-projections.html)
- Year-to-year swings: capture moves by about ±4 Mt, mainly with El Niño and the Peruvian anchovy catch. That shifts the share by roughly ±1 pp in a given year. The 2024-2033 Outlook assumed 89 Mt of capture in El Niño years versus 94 Mt otherwise. [eurofish](https://eurofish.dk/?p=8431)
- If the 2035 projection of 56% is simply extended at 0.3-0.4 pp a year, 2040 comes out around 57.5-58%. This is my arithmetic, not an official figure.

## 5. Other forecasts
- No prediction market on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold matches this question. The markets supplied (Mississippi catfish, broilers and others) are not relevant.
- Expert projections: OECD-FAO gives 56% for 2034 and for 2035. FAO gives 54% for 2032 (from SOFIA 2024) and, from SOFIA 2026, 119 Mt aquaculture against about 95 Mt capture in 2034, which is about 55.6%. A Statista-cited report gives just under 53% for 2030. [Statista](https://statista.com/statistics/755939/share-of-fish-production-worldwide-by-type)
- I found no official or academic projection that goes out to 2040.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Each year in June or July, a new OECD-FAO Outlook appears (2027-2036, then 2028-2037, and so on). The 2031-2040 edition, around 2031, would be the first to include 2040.
- FAO's SOFIA reports come out every two years: 2028, 2030 and so on.
- The El Niño of 2026-27 and its effect on Peru's anchovy quotas could cause a short-lived jump in the share.
- Other things that could move the trend: China's aquaculture policy, since its share is falling, and growth in India and Viet Nam. Also feed constraints (fishmeal and fish oil) and disease outbreaks.
- If the OECD changes its dataset, or another body takes over the reporting, the question could be annulled or moved to a different source.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left: about 13 years. The question resolves around 2040-01-01, so the "2040" value will in practice be an OECD-FAO Outlook estimate or projection for 2040, from roughly the 2030s editions, rather than final observed data.

(b) Latest known value: the question background gives 52.1% aquaculture for 2024 (modelled, 2023-2032 dataset). SOFIA 2026 gives about 53% for 2024, and the 2026-2035 Outlook gives 53% for 2023-25.

(c) If nothing changed: about 52-53%.

(d) If the current trend continued: the Outlooks project about 56% by 2034-2035, a pace of about 0.3-0.4 pp a year. A straight-line extension gives about 57.5-58% in 2040.
- Another check: if aquaculture grows about 1.5% a year from 121 Mt in 2035 and capture stays near 95 Mt, the 2040 share is about 57.8%.
- Successive Outlook editions have revised the share upward slightly.

(e) Historical variation: over the 2000s-2010s the share rose about 1 pp a year. Growth has slowed recently. Capture swings driven by El Niño can move a single year's share by about ±1 pp. China statistical revisions have shifted levels by several percent in the past.

(f) Expert and market expectations:
- OECD-FAO and SOFIA project 56% by 2034-2035.
- No source gives a figure for 2040.
- No prediction markets cover this question.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- **Low:** China's aquaculture stagnates or its statistics are revised down, disease or environmental limits bite, and capture recovers strongly with good anchovy years. This would leave the share around 53-54%.
- **High:** rapid aquaculture expansion in Africa, South Asia and offshore farming, combined with climate-driven capture declines or a strong El Niño in 2040. This would push the share to 62-65%.

(a) Time left: about 13 years. The 2040 value will be read around January 2040. By then it will most likely still be a modelled figure from the latest OECD-FAO Outlook, not an observed one.

(b) Latest known value: 52.1% aquaculture share for 2024 (a modelled year in the 2023-2032 dataset). Newer sources agree: SOFIA 2026 and the 2026-2035 Outlook both put the share at about 53% for 2023-25.

(c) If nothing changed: about 53%.

(d) If the current trend continued: the Outlooks project 56% by 2034-2035, rising about 0.3-0.4 percentage points a year. Extending that line gives about 57.5-58.5% in 2040. Two things point slightly higher:
- Each Outlook edition has revised its projections upward.
- Observed growth in the 2010s was about 0.9 percentage points a year.

(e) Historical variation: over 13 years the share has moved by about 5-10 percentage points. In single years, El Niño-driven swings in Peru's anchovy catch can move it by about 1 percentage point. Data revisions, such as the China statistics revisions, have shifted levels by a few points.

(f) Experts and markets: the OECD-FAO and SOFIA projections give 56% for 2034-2035. Nobody has published a share for 2040. No prediction market covers this question.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- Low: China's aquaculture stagnates under environmental limits and disease, global growth falls to about 1% a year, and capture rises with good stocks and favourable conditions. The share would then end near 54-55%.
- High: aquaculture expands quickly in Africa, South Asia and Latin America while warming and overfishing push capture down to about 80 Mt. The share would then reach 63-65%.
